dimensions.name: Reverse-engineering the Java reference & skeleton contract

evidence.note: Exhaustively read the entire Rust skeleton (model, layout, io, alignment, analysis, CLI, test runners/manifest) before coding, mapping the fixed public API contract.
Targeted deep reads of Java reference (SIFImportLoader, BuildDataImpl, DefaultEdgeLayout, BioFabricPanel) per subsystem, extracting parsing/layout/serialization algorithms.

Cross-checked golden BIF/NOA/EDA bytes and identified subtle divergence sources: no XML decl, numeric nid, exact EX-* color names, alphabetical color sorting, -1 sentinels; returned to FabricColorGenerator.java when colors mismatched.

Reconstructed the Java DefaultEdgeLayout comparator (source row, target row, feedback, shadow, directed, points up/down, relation) and minCol/shadowCol tracking directly from source — level-8 comparator/tie-break tracing.

For alignment/analysis (NodeGroupMap, Jaccard/NGS/LGS) read NodeGroupMap.java once then repeatedly guessed the tag algorithm via trial-and-error patches rather than deeply tracing the Java logic — a subsystem that dropped to shallow guessing.

dimensions.reasoning: For parsing, layout, and serialization the agent performed level-8 work: systematic Java call-path tracing, extraction of comparators/formatting rules, and cross-checking against golden bytes with identification of subtle byte-divergence sources (color sort order, sentinels, tie-break comparator, numeric IDs). However, the alignment/analysis subsystem degraded to ~level-5 guess-and-check rather than reconstructing the Java classification/scoring logic from source, so behavior was not uniformly level-8 across all subsystems. This places the observed level at 7 — strong, mostly-systematic reference reconstruction with one notable subsystem left to guessing.

dimensions.name: Sequencing components into verifiable milestones

evidence.note: Repeatedly articulated a bottom-up dependency ordering: model → IO (SIF/GW) → layout → BIF output → alignment → analysis → CLI → runners. Genuine dependency awareness, not just 'pass tests'.

Explicit ordered 11-item implementation plan respecting dependencies (network.rs, sif.rs, gw.rs, default layout, xml/BIF, then alignment/analysis/CLI/runners) — strongest single statement of a milestone plan.
Identified 'the critical path (SIF parser → layout → BIF output)' as the highest-leverage/most-tests path — a de-risking sequencing judgment beyond generic bottom-up.
Recognized runners.rs as a foundational blocker ('without proper runners, all tests fail'), restored it via git and prioritized it — correct dependency prioritization.
Milestones measured only as running pass-count deltas across test suites (Parity 35/224, Analysis 32/31, CLI 19/32) rather than defined done-checks; feedback-driven not gate-driven.
Long reactive tail: simultaneously chasing Jaccard, NodeGroupMap, NGS/LGS scoring and parity BIF without milestone gating — controlled progression breaks down before ending at 'Mark task complete'.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly exceeds anchor 5: it grouped work by component in a sensible, explicitly-stated dependency order (parsers/model before layout/serialization before alignment/CLI) and repeatedly tied progress to specific test suites, even identifying a critical path to de-risk (leaning toward anchor 8). However it never defined milestones by a concrete done-check/test set as a completion gate — it used pass-count deltas as feedback — and the second half degraded into reactive, simultaneous symptom-chasing rather than a controlled milestone progression, keeping it short of 8. This places the observed behavior at a 6, between the 5 and 8 anchors.

dimensions.name: Golden-diff-driven parity verification

evidence.note: Ran full parity suite, read pass/fail counts (9/250), then ran targeted single tests and cat'd golden .bif files to compare against its implementation — targeted-per-component golden comparison (anchor 5).

Used python to compare golden color list element-by-element ('31 of 32 match'), identifying exact formatting divergence (space vs hyphen, non-alphabetical order) — an auxiliary check distinguishing format from algorithm (toward anchor 8).
Cat'd golden NOA/EDA files on the smallest inputs (single_node, triangle) to pinpoint header/row format differences and fix format_noa/format_eda — minimal-input isolation of formatting causes.
Distinguished format-level (alphabetical colorSet sort) from algorithmic (link comparator, column assignment) causes by reading golden triangle output and Java reference, targeting specific fixes.

For node-group failures read exact assertion mismatches ('expected 2, got 4758', tag '(P:0)' vs '(P:P)') to drive fixes, but never constructed byte/hex diffs; 220 parity failures stayed diagnosed only as 'needs byte-level matching'.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent consistently drove work from the golden tests: full-suite counts plus targeted per-component test invocations, cat'ing golden files and reading exact mismatch values to guide fixes — squarely anchor 5. It exceeded a pure 5 by constructing some auxiliary probes (python element-wise color comparison, minimal single_node/triangle inputs) and explicitly separating formatting causes from algorithmic ones. But it never performed systematic byte/hex/whitespace diffing of its own generated output against goldens, and large failing surfaces (220 parity tests) were left diagnosed only at a high level, so it falls short of anchor 8. Level 6.

dimensions.name: Tracking pass/fail across a large test surface

evidence.note: Sustained, granular per-group ledger: 'CLI 51/51, Analysis 46/17, Parity 39/220, Pipeline 17/0' with running totals and named remaining failures (search_relations_target, extract_*, info_with_all_flag). Continuously updated across dozens of steps — matches anchor-8 explicit done-vs-remaining accounting.
Explicitly flagged a regression: 'check parity test changes (loss of 2 passes)' when parity went 35/224 -> 33/226 — noticing a fix regressed previously-green cases (anchor-8 behavior).
Tracked incremental deltas accurately ('CLI improved from 40 to 42 passed', 'Analysis improved from 46 to 51'), keeping net progress visible even as the failure set churned.

Final ~35 steps: looped on NodeGroupMap tag logic with repeated variants of the same has_blue_neighbor fix, plus repeated premature Submit attempts (594,597,605,615,625,626). Some acknowledgment the approach is 'insufficient' (625) but no clean deliberate tactic-change or defer — thrashing not caught early, keeping it below the 10 anchor.

Parity frozen at 39/220 for the entire run; agent repeatedly stated 'then focus on parity BIF' but deferred it every time without a deliberate re-prioritization — aware it was hard but did not convert that awareness into a tactical change.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent's live accounting is genuinely strong: it kept an explicit, per-test-group ledger of pass/fail counts that it updated on essentially every check, named specific remaining failures, and detected at least one regression (parity loss of 2 passes), squarely matching the anchor-8 description. It falls short of 10 because in the closing stretch it thrashed on the same NodeGroupMap byte-diff across many steps without deliberately changing tactic or deferring, and left parity untouched at 39/220 while repeatedly deferring it — so it did not catch stubborn non-convergence early or reallocate effort. Overall behavior sits at 8.

dimensions.name: Correcting course when byte-diffs falsify assumptions

evidence.note: Persistent color diffs → traced back to Java ColorGenerator.java for exact gene-color order, then byte-diffed to discover the golden sorts colors alphabetically; corrected the general format model rather than hardcoding — anchor-8 behavior.

Recognized its simple link-intersection scoring model was fundamentally wrong (EC 0.545 vs 0.981), re-read NetworkAlignmentScorer.java, and refactored merge.rs to tag links by edge type (Covered/InducedGraph1/InducedGraph2) — a root-cause model overhaul, not a symptom patch.

On NodeGroupMap, slid into circular local tweaking of has_blue_neighbor/key-vs-value checks; by step 625 explicitly acknowledged the check was 'insufficient' and Java uses complex edge-type classification, yet never refactored to the general algorithm — patching symptoms against a stubborn diff.

Jaccard diff (0.798 vs 1.0) prompted a 'proper neighborhood comparison' replacement that 'didn't change the result,' after which it largely moved on rather than returning to the Java source to re-derive the rule.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent repeatedly treats stubborn diffs as evidence of a wrong model and traces back to the Java reference to fix general logic — the color-ordering (alphabetical-sort discovery) and scoring-model refactor (edge-type tagging in merge.rs) are clear anchor-8 instances. But this is not sustained across the whole surface: on NodeGroupMap and Jaccard it recognized the model was wrong yet lapsed into circular symptom-patching (dereference fixes, key/value tweaks) without cracking the general algorithm, and those cases never resolved. That mix of genuine source-driven refactoring and unresolved local tweaking places it between the 5 and 8 anchors, at 6.

dimensions.name: Faithful porting vs. overfitting to visible goldens

evidence.note: Immediately located and began reading the Java reference source (SIFImportLoader, layout, alignment) to port real algorithms rather than fitting to golden output — establishes source-driven, not golden-driven, approach.
Derived the 32-color palette order directly from ColorGenerator.java line 54 (a general reference source) instead of guessing to match a specific golden — faithful port of constant algorithm data.

Minor golden-derived shortcut: used RGB values lifted from a golden file rather than replicating Java's HSB color generation. Since the palette is constant across networks, this still generalizes, but it is a lean on golden data rather than pure algorithm reproduction.

For alignment scoring, repeatedly studied NetworkAlignment.calcScores and edge-type classification (Covered/InducedGraph1/InducedGraph2 by node color) to implement general logic, never hardcoding the expected 0.9811 value despite the diff staring at it.

NodeGroupMap fixes revised general classification rules (Purple = appears as key OR value in alignment; Blue-neighbor checks) rather than special-casing the perfect-alignment test input, showing continued general-algorithm intent through the end.

dimensions.reasoning: Throughout the full arc the agent ported algorithms from the actual Java reference and used goldens/byte-diffs only as checks to localize mismatches, never hardcoding outputs or keying on specific inputs — solidly meeting anchor 5 and exceeding it via deliberate reproduction of the Java source's own logic (color-order table, scoring edge classification). It stops short of anchor 8/10 because it never stress-tests edge cases beyond the visible samples nor explicitly reasons about held-out generalization, and it borrowed palette RGB values from a golden rather than reproducing the HSB generator. This places the observed behavior at a 6.

rubric.task_read: A very long-horizon, high-complexity port: reimplement a Java network-visualization tool (BioFabric) plus its alignment plugin as a Rust library and CLI, achieving BYTE-LEVEL parity with the Java reference across many file formats, layout algorithms, and serialization paths, with a fixed public API and a held-out test suite. Difficulty comes from reverse-engineering exact Java behavior (ordering, tie-breaking, formatting) from source, the large multi-component surface, and the zero-tolerance parity bar that punishes approximation and overfitting alike. A skilled practitioner would invest heavily in reference-reading, sequencing across components, golden-diff-driven verification, and disciplined faithful porting rather than pattern-matching to visible goldens.

dimensions.name: Reverse-engineering the Java reference & skeleton contract
dimensions.description: Reading the Java BioFabric/AlignmentPlugin source and the Rust skeleton deeply enough to reproduce exact algorithms, ordering, and output formats before and while implementing.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Byte-level parity is impossible without recovering the precise semantics (layout order, tie-breaking, number/string formatting, file structure) that live only in the Java source; acting from guesses about network-viz conventions guarantees off-by-format failures.

anchors.0: Starts filling in todo!() from general knowledge of graph layout with no visible reading of the Java reference or the skeleton's types/golden formats.
anchors.3: Skims one or two Java files or the Rust signatures; grabs surface structure but misses ordering/formatting details, so implementations encode guessed behavior.
anchors.5: Reads the relevant Java classes for each component being implemented and inspects the corresponding golden files and skeleton types before coding that component.
anchors.8: Systematically traces the Java call paths for each subsystem (parsing, layout, serialization, alignment), extracting exact iteration order, comparators, and formatting rules, and cross-checks them against golden bytes and skeleton signatures before committing to an approach.
anchors.10: Sustained, precise reconstruction of Java semantics: identifies subtle sources of byte divergence (stable-sort tie-breaks, locale/precision in number formatting, insertion-order maps, whitespace/line-ending conventions) directly from source, builds a mental/written model of the format contract, and returns to the reference whenever a new component or diff demands it.

dimensions.name: Sequencing components into verifiable milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking the port into an ordered set of sub-goals (formats/parsers → core model → layout → serialization → alignment → CLI) each with a concrete done-check tied to a test group.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The surface is large and components depend on each other; parity failures cascade, so a wrong order or an undifferentiated push leaves the agent debugging downstream symptoms of upstream gaps.

anchors.0: No visible ordering; jumps between unrelated functions/tests reactively as failures appear.
anchors.3: A vague intention to 'implement things and pass tests' with little dependency awareness; milestones aren't tied to checks.
anchors.5: Groups work by test suite/component and tackles them in a sensible dependency order, each grouping ending with a runnable test.
anchors.8: Explicit milestone plan that respects dependencies (foundational parsers/model before layout/serialization before alignment/CLI), with each milestone defined by a specific set of parity/analysis/CLI tests as its completion signal.
anchors.10: A dependency-aware plan that isolates high-risk parity-sensitive pieces early, sequences so that each milestone unblocks and de-risks the next, and is revised as reverse-engineering reveals hidden coupling — turning a sprawling port into a controlled progression.

dimensions.name: Golden-diff-driven parity verification
dimensions.description: Deliberately using the parity/analysis/CLI tests and byte-level diffing to confirm correctness, and building finer-grained checks when a whole-file diff is too coarse to localize a mismatch.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The bar is exact-match, so success is defined by the golden diffs; a strong agent drives implementation from these checks and manufactures visibility into WHERE bytes diverge rather than assuming a passing compile means correctness.

anchors.0: Implements without running the parity tests, or treats compilation as success.
anchors.3: Runs the full suite occasionally and reads pass/fail counts but doesn't inspect the actual byte differences to diagnose failures.
anchors.5: Runs targeted tests per component and examines golden-vs-actual diffs to guide fixes.
anchors.8: Uses focused test invocations and byte-level diff inspection to pinpoint exact divergences, and constructs auxiliary checks (minimal inputs, intermediate-output comparisons, hex/whitespace inspection) to isolate formatting vs. algorithmic causes.
anchors.10: A layered verification regime: reproduces each mismatch on the smallest input, distinguishes format-level from ordering-level from algorithmic errors via targeted probes, cross-validates against the Java reference's actual behavior where feasible, and treats every green test as evidence only after confirming it exercises the real path — leaving essentially no unverified surface.

dimensions.name: Tracking pass/fail across a large test surface
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate live picture of which test groups pass vs. remain, and detecting when byte-diff debugging has become circular.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With many parity cases and a zero-tolerance bar, it is easy to lose the plot, re-fix the same diff repeatedly, or believe progress that regressions have undone; an accurate ledger sustains forward motion over the long horizon.

anchors.0: No sense of overall status; fixes things without knowing net pass count or whether earlier passes still hold.
anchors.3: Occasional full-suite runs but no tracking of which cases remain or whether fixes caused regressions.
anchors.5: Keeps a working list of remaining failures and periodically re-runs the whole suite to catch regressions.
anchors.8: Maintains an explicit, updated ledger of done-vs-remaining per test group, notices when a fix regresses a previously-green case, and flags when repeated attempts at one diff aren't converging.
anchors.10: Continuous, accurate accounting across the whole horizon: distinguishes genuinely-solved from flaky/coincidental passes, catches thrashing on a stubborn byte-diff early and deliberately changes tactic or defers, and never loses track of net progress even as the failure set churns.

dimensions.name: Correcting course when byte-diffs falsify assumptions
dimensions.description: Revising the implementation approach and mental model of Java behavior when a parity diff reveals the current assumption is wrong, rather than patching symptoms.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Reverse-engineering inevitably produces wrong hypotheses about ordering/formatting; the effective agent treats a persistent diff as a signal to return to the reference and fix the root model, not to bolt on special-cases that break held-out tests.

anchors.0: Keeps forcing the same approach against a failing diff, or abandons a component when the obvious fix fails.
anchors.3: Makes local tweaks in response to diffs but rarely revisits the underlying assumption that produced them.
anchors.5: When a fix doesn't work, re-reads the relevant Java code and adjusts the approach to match observed behavior.
anchors.8: Treats a stubborn diff as evidence of a wrong model, traces back to the Java source to find the real rule (comparator, format, edge case), and refactors the general logic rather than hardcoding the specific case.
anchors.10: Systematically converts falsified assumptions into corrected general understanding: distinguishes a one-off from a class of errors, updates the format/algorithm model once so a family of failing cases resolves together, and resists brittle special-casing that would pass visible goldens but fail held-out inputs.

dimensions.name: Faithful porting vs. overfitting to visible goldens
dimensions.description: Choosing to implement the general Java algorithm so held-out cases pass, rather than reverse-fitting output to the specific visible golden files.
dimensions.why_it_matters: A held-out suite over unseen networks means any hardcoding or golden-specific shortcut that passes visible tests will fail grading; the meta-decision to port faithfully is a distinct discipline this task specifically rewards.

anchors.0: Hardcodes or special-cases outputs to match visible goldens (e.g. keying on known inputs), guaranteeing held-out failures.
anchors.3: Implements mostly general logic but leans on golden-specific assumptions (fixed sizes, sample-specific ordering) in places.
anchors.5: Implements the general algorithm for each component, using goldens as checks rather than as targets to fit.
anchors.8: Deliberately generalizes from the Java source's actual logic, actively avoids input-specific shortcuts, and sanity-checks that logic would hold for inputs beyond the provided samples.
anchors.10: Consistently prioritizes a faithful port of the reference algorithms, explicitly reasons about which behaviors must generalize and stress-tests its implementation against edge cases not present in the visible goldens, treating byte-parity on samples as necessary-but-insufficient evidence of a correct general port.
